section_summary: This section documents inter-agency deliberations between the Department of State and the Department of the Army from December 1947 to February 1948 concerning policy papers SANACC 381/1, 381/2, and 384 on Japanese economic recovery. The papers reveal differing perspectives on the scope of long-range economic planning, U.S. aid commitments, and the extent of occupation controls, as well as joint opposition to congressional requests to declassify Far Eastern Commission policy paper FEC 230 on deconcentration. Accompanying political adviser despatches from Tokyo report on Japan's severe budgetary deficit, inflation, and tax collection problems discussed with Economic Stabilization Board leaders Hiroo Wada and Shigeto Tsuru, alongside broader policy discussions regarding industrial socialization across occupied Germany and Japan.

subfiles.about: Provides line-by-line editorial and substantive criticisms of SANACC 381/1 regarding FEC responsibilities under the Japanese economic recovery plan.
subfiles.summary: Criticizes SANACC 381/1 for wordiness and recommends drafting changes concerning FEC review powers, post-treaty U.S. controls, shipping restrictions, and avoiding friction with SCAP.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on SANACC 381/1

subfiles.about: Advocates embedding Japanese economic recovery within a comprehensive regional recovery program for the Far East.
subfiles.summary: Argues Japanese recovery requires restoring trade across Asia, proposing a regional Far Eastern Marshall Plan to secure Asian cooperation and counter Soviet influence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Economic Recovery in Japan (SANACC 381/1 and 381/2)

subfiles.about: Summarizes responses to questions from General McCoy regarding declassification of FEC 230 and SWNCC 302/2.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes positions on congressional inquiries and FEC action regarding declassification of FEC 230 and SWNCC 302/2, enclosing related correspondence.
subfiles.title: Letter to Major General Frank R. McCoy regarding Declassification of FEC 230

subfiles.about: States the State Department's reasons for opposing the declassification and publication of FEC 230 and SWNCC 302/2.
subfiles.summary: Details objections to declassifying unfinalized policy papers, citing public confusion, violation of FEC customs, and prejudice to pending policy negotiations (includes duplicate copy).
subfiles.title: Letter to Gordon Gray regarding Declassification of FEC 230 and SWNCC 302/2

subfiles.about: Presents an Army Department compromise proposal on SANACC 384 regarding Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Submits compromise papers proposing that a revised State paper be submitted to FEC while an amended Army paper guides General MacArthur and is released publicly.
subfiles.title: Letter to Frank G. Wisner regarding SANACC 384, 'The Economic Recovery of Japan'

subfiles.about: Transmits Under Secretary Draper's letter and compromise proposals on SANACC 384.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Draper's signed letter and enclosures on SANACC 384, superseding an earlier informal draft.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Frank G. Wisner Transmitting Letter from Under Secretary Draper

subfiles.about: Transmits and summarizes a memorandum of conversation with Shigeto Tsuru concerning Japanese economic stabilization and occupation problems.
subfiles.summary: Sebald transmits Lawrence's memorandum of conversation with Shigeto Tsuru detailing Japan's trade deficit, inflation, tax collection failures, and urgent need for 400 million dollars in 1948 U.S. aid. Tsuru also warns against SCAP's excessive involvement in administrative operating details.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1486: Conversation with Shigeto Tsuru, Deputy Director-General of the Economic Stabilization Board

subfiles.about: Outlines draft conclusions on accelerating Japanese economic self-support under paragraph 4 of FEC 014/10.
subfiles.summary: Proposes accelerating implementation of FEC 014/10 to promote Japanese self-support while obtaining international cooperation and preventing prejudicial burdens.
subfiles.title: Draft Conclusions on Implementation of FEC 014/10

subfiles.about: Explains procedure and revisions to conclusions and discussion in SANACC 381/2 on Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Outlines changes to SANACC 381/2 and recommends securing tentative SANACC approval before transmitting the paper to SCAP for concurrence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on SANACC 381/2

subfiles.about: Reports on a conversation with Butterworth regarding State-Army negotiations and economic policy toward Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of Financial and Development Policy
subfiles.summary: Reports Butterworth's view that normal commerce rather than intergovernmental planning will spur recovery, and notes Dutch and Pakistani interest in Japanese textiles.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Conversation with Mr. Butterworth, FE
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin and Roswell H. Whitman

subfiles.about: Submits Fearey's memorandum on SANACC 381/2 along with an alternative shortened draft of conclusions.
keywords: Office of Financial and Development Policy
subfiles.summary: Submits Fearey's memorandum and recommends agreeing to Butterworth's specific changes to the OE draft rather than pursuing a shortened paper.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on SANACC 381/2

subfiles.about: Examines fundamental differences between FE and OE regarding SANACC 381/2, incorporating Tabs A through D.
subfiles.summary: Fearey contrasts FE's emphasis on private initiative with OE's insistence on comprehensive long-range planning and advance U.S. aid commitments. The document includes Butterworth's specific comments (Tab A), shortened draft conclusions (Tab B), Maxwell Hamilton's written views (Tab C), and McDiarmid's analysis of the Army's 180 million dollar rehabilitation request (Tab D).
subfiles.title: Memorandum on SANACC 381/2, 'Self-Support of the Japanese Economy', with Tabs A-D

subfiles.about: Provides briefing points for a meeting with Senator Knowland opposing declassification of FEC 230.
subfiles.from: Office of the Assistant Secretary for Occupied Areas
subfiles.summary: Outlines arguments against declassifying FEC 230, emphasizing dangerous international precedents, impending revisions, and the risk of misleading the public.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Points and Background for Proposed Conversation with Senator Knowland re Request for Declassification of FEC 230

subfiles.about: Raises questions regarding U.S. policy on socialization in occupied areas under draft SWNCC 302/2, attaching 1947 correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Queries whether top-level policy guidance on industrial socialization in occupied areas is required, attaching a January 1947 letter exchange between Howard Petersen and General Hilldring regarding Germany.
subfiles.title: Letter to Charles E. Saltzman regarding Socialization in Occupied Areas (with Enclosures)

subfiles.about: Advises against issuing a comprehensive policy statement on public ownership in occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: Recommends against preparing an overall policy paper on socialization, noting existing German directives suffice and that public ownership in revised FEC 230 should remain restricted to non-competitive ex-Zaibatsu concerns (includes draft page).
subfiles.title: Memorandum on U. S. Policy on Public Ownership in Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: Sends an interim reply regarding Gray's inquiry on public ownership policy in occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: Informs Gray that State is actively studying whether further policy statements on public ownership are needed before deciding on SANACC submission.
subfiles.title: Letter to Gordon Gray regarding Policy on Public Ownership in Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: Transmits Gray's letter and Saltzman's interim reply concerning public ownership in occupied areas to OE.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Gray's letter and Saltzman's reply, requesting that OE study the need for revised policy statements on public ownership.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on U. S. Policy on Public Ownership in Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: Recommends postponing discussions on public ownership in Japan pending George F. Kennan's return.
subfiles.summary: Advises Gray to defer consideration of paragraph 8b of draft SWNCC 302/2 and public ownership in Japan until George F. Kennan returns from his mission.
subfiles.title: Letter to Gordon Gray regarding Policy on Public Ownership in Japan

subfiles.about: Provides the text of JCS 1067 (Revised) paragraph 21c regarding public ownership in Germany.
subfiles.summary: Instructs the Military Governor to refrain from interfering in German public ownership decisions made through democratic processes, while safeguarding foreign-owned property.
subfiles.title: Extract of JCS 1067 (Revised), Paragraph 21c

subfiles.about: Provides the text of draft SWNCC 302/2 paragraph 8b on governmental acquisition of divested Japanese enterprises.
subfiles.summary: Permits Japanese governments to acquire divested holdings in excessive economic concentrations and non-competitive utilities unsuitable for dissolution.
subfiles.title: Extract of Draft Revision of SWNCC 302/2, Paragraph 8b
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Reports observations of Hiroo Wada and Shigeto Tsuru regarding Japanese finances, SCAP involvement, and coal output.
subfiles.summary: Reports Wada's and Tsuru's concerns over Japanese budget deficits, the need for expert financial advisers in SCAP, winter coal production gains, and Diet passage of industrial decentralization legislation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1495: Observations of Members of the Economic Stabilization Board

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of McCoy's letter regarding Senator Knowland's request to declassify FEC 230.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges McCoy's letter on FEC 230 declassification and confirms forwarding its contents to Senator Knowland.
subfiles.title: Letter to Major General Frank R. McCoy regarding Declassification of FEC 230

subfiles.about: Explains why the Far Eastern Commission chairman considers declassification of FEC 230 inadvisable.
subfiles.summary: General McCoy argues against declassifying FEC 230, stating it would establish a damaging diplomatic precedent, confuse the public with obsolete policy, and hinder negotiations on revised deconcentration policy.
subfiles.title: Letter to Charles E. Saltzman regarding Declassification of FEC 230
